correctness.rationale: The exact three-ball formula leads by max^2<=sum of squares and Cauchy-Schwarz to energy bound (1); for a norm-maximizer with n>=10^6(m+1)^6 this yields b<=20(m+1)/sqrt(n), m-X^2<=900(m+1)^4/n, and hence all class-A values >1/(2sqrt(m)). All radius choices strictly stabilize to class-A identity and class-B radius-one averaging. The resulting linear map has mean-zero singular values 1 and (m+1)^-1, and a positive 2x2 block of trace tau and determinant (m+1)^-2. Its unique Perron eigenvector gives the full norm and signs. Expanding the quadratic formula verifies the n^-1 correction. Checker runs were finite diagnostics, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Strong L2 norm evaluation for centered maximal graph averages is a natural quantitative functional-analysis problem established in the cited literature. An entire infinite tail of unbalanced bicliques has an exact radical and a unique extremizing modulus, despite nonlinear competition among three averaging radii at each vertex. The theorem proves selector stabilization and a two-term norm asymptotic with correction rather than merely giving a lower bound or small-graph numerics. The conservative cutoff is explicit and legitimate, but not sharp.
